title: Open-source SaaS starter
summary: One pick per layer for a product you intend to run yourself, chosen so the whole set can sit on a single server if it has to.

items.note: Postgres with auth, storage, and generated APIs on top, so the first version does not need a bespoke backend.
Worth taking even alongside a backend that offers auth, if the app is already a Next.js app and you want sessions handled in it.
Copied into the repo rather than installed, so the component code stays yours to change.
Cookie-free, which keeps the consent-banner work off the backlog.
Gives you a Heroku-shaped workflow on a server you rent, which is the usual reason this list exists.

title: Self-hosted support desk
summary: Talking to customers without a per-seat subscription. Pick one of the first three rather than all of them.

items.note: The broadest of the three: live chat widget plus email and social channels in one inbox.
Closer to a classic help desk, with stronger ticket workflow than chat.
Runs on ordinary PHP hosting, which makes it the cheapest of the three to keep alive.
For the announcements and onboarding sequences a support tool does not cover.

title: Product data stack
summary: Knowing what users do, and being able to ask questions the dashboard did not anticipate.

items.note: Lighter than Plausible to run: one database rather than two.
Points at the database you already have and gives non-engineers a way to ask it questions.
Only worth adding once event volume makes queries against the app database slow. Not a day-one component.
